02 / Three useful representations.

COG vs Zarr vs Virtual Zarr.

COG.

Physical raster layout.

Arrange pixels and overviews for raster access.

Physical Zarr.

Physical array layout.

Arrange chunks across the dimensions you need.

Virtual Zarr.

Logical array layout.

Reference compatible chunks already in the archive.

No universal winner.These are architectural choices, not mutually exclusive ecosystems.

06 / Demo recipe.

Demo. Building the Virtual Store.

◇ Adapted code. Not executed here.Three-file local subset. Full setup and validation are in notes.
Python 3.12 / VirtualiZarr 2.0.1 / Icechunk 1.1.1
vds = open_virtual_mfdataset(
    urls, registry=registry, parser=HDFParser(),
    combine="nested", concat_dim="time",
    coords="minimal", compat="equals",
    loadable_variables=["time", "lat", "lon"],
    decode_times=True,
)
session = build_repo.writable_session("main")
vds.vz.to_icechunk(session.store)
snapshot_id = session.commit("NLDAS-3 daily subset")

07 / Demo recipe.

Demo. xarray to Analysis.

◇ Adapted code. Not executed here.Published Icechunk path. Source and store credentials are configured separately.
Read-only session / xarray 2025.6.0 / Zarr format 3
session = repo.readonly_session("main")
ds = xr.open_zarr(session.store, consolidated=False,
                  zarr_format=3, chunks={})
point = ds["Tair"].sel(
    lat=40.0, lon=-100.0, method="nearest")
series = point.sel(time=slice("2020-01-01", "2020-01-31"))
assert series.attrs.get("units") == "K"
series = series.compute()
series.plot()
Lazy selection is not retrieval. .compute() is the execution boundary.

11 / Limits are part of the design.

Where Virtual Zarr Breaks Down.

◇ General engineering risks. Not observed failures here.
01

Wrong chunk geometry.

Long point histories can intersect many broad spatial chunks.

Test a different physical layout for the hot workload.

02

Request amplification.

Many small objects or fragmented reads can dominate access.

Measure requests, useful bytes and concurrency.

03

Encoding or schema mismatch.

Codecs, fill values, scales or coordinates may not align.

Fail validation rather than silently combining.

04

Source identity changes.

Replaced, deleted or restricted source objects can break reads.

Pin identities, authorize both layers and monitor drift.

The hard limit.A logical representation cannot repair a physical layout mismatch.
VirtualiZarr / Icechunk implementation · Co-Working Group limitations, not NASA policy12 / 14
12 / Recommendations, not deployment claims.

Production Design Patterns.

01

Start from the query.

Inspect source layout and benchmark the real workload.

02

Make equivalence testable.

Compare decoded values, coordinates, units and masks.

03

Version both layers.

Record source identity and reference snapshot. Name an owner.

04

Operate the read path.

Control access, observe requests and detect broken references.

A proposed hybrid.

Materialize where repeated demand justifies it.

Keep discovery separate.An access URL identifies a store. It does not construct its references.
Workload-first recommendations · NASA Co-Working Group report · URL proposal caveats in notes13 / 14
13 / Takeaways.

Takeaways.

01

Cloud-native access does not always require a full rewrite.

02

Each representation puts costs in different places.

03

Source layout must fit the access pattern.

04

Less duplication still requires operational care.

Choose the workflow.
Then choose the representation.

Conclusion · COG, physical Zarr and virtual representations remain complementary options14 / 14
